title: Feature-detect the installed CLI; do not program against GitHub main
summary: The installed command surface is the runtime authority. Record colab version, inspect colab <command> -h, and adapt only to flags actually present. A live google-colab-cli 0.6.0 installation rejected colab exec --env and its colab new help did not expose --high-mem, while later upstream main documentation advertises --high-mem. This is a concrete example of documentation/version drift: never make a managed-compute adapter depend on a flag because current main or a newer design document mentions it.
evidence_note: Live project qualification on Linux with google-colab-cli 0.6.0; PyPI records 0.6.0 as released 2026-06-16. Current upstream GitHub main, consulted 2026-09-02, documents --high-mem on new/run/ssh, demonstrating why installed-help probing is necessary.
invariants: Persist the installed CLI version as execution evidence.
Probe subcommand help before emitting optional flags.
Unsupported provider flags must be omitted while the generic resource requirement remains in the job contract.
Do not silently downgrade a hard requirement; if the provider cannot express it, verify it in the worker or reject before work.
